name: agent-prompt
title: Agent prompt
description: Connect a coding agent over MCP: the agent at work on top, the prompt in a box that opens, then Copy prompt with the one-click installs and the API call beside it. The agent signs in with OAuth, so no key is shown.
use_for: The agents page, whenever an agent is connected.
never: Pasting an API key into the prompt
Two copy buttons as the page's main action
source: conare-web app/components/console/agents/Connect.vue, agents/ConnectViz.vue, agent/Split.vue (take 2), app/composables/useAgentPrompt.ts, app/assets/css/console2.css (.v2-agentwork, .v2-promptbox, .v2-split), docs-viz.css
body:
Build the prompt in your app (it names the MCP server and the namespaces connected) and pass it with the request
`code`. `installs` are the one-click links the prompt can't do (Cursor's and VS Code's install links); without them the
split has no arrow. `AgentWindow` plays the website's agent window once as it renders; `AgentSplit` works on its own.
The dark panel carries the grain and a seeded sheet of cells (`cell-burst`) under the agent's window.

examples.content:
<script setup lang="ts">
import AgentPrompt from '@/components/product/AgentPrompt.vue'
// The panel the agents page opens, for a sample team with three namespaces connected: the agent at work, the prompt,
// Copy prompt with the one-click installs, and the API call.
const MCP = 'https://api.conare.ai/v1/mcp'
const prompt = `Connect Conare and search the data I connected.

1. Check whether you have Conare's MCP tools (search, save, fetch, list_namespaces). If not, add the server:
   - Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user conare ${MCP}
     Then ask me to run /mcp, choose conare and sign in.
   - Codex: codex mcp add conare --url ${MCP}
     Then ask me to run: codex mcp login conare
   - Cursor: add "conare": {"url": "${MCP}"} under "mcpServers" in ~/.cursor/mcp.json, then ask me to sign in from Cursor's MCP settings.
   - Any other client: it is a remote MCP server at ${MCP} and sign-in is OAuth.
   If the tools still don't appear after I sign in, ask me to restart this session and paste this prompt again.
2. List my namespaces with list_namespaces. I connected contracts, slack, crm.
3. Search Conare for a question those documents answer, such as a recent decision or a contract term. Show me the answer and the documents it came from.
4. From now on, search Conare before you answer questions about my company's work.`
const code = `curl https://api.conare.ai/v1/query \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONARE_API_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"query": "how do refunds work?", "top_k": 5}'`
const installs = [
  { label: 'Add to Cursor', href: '#cursor' },
  { label: 'Add to VS Code', href: '#vscode' },
]
</script>

<template>
  <AgentPrompt :prompt="prompt" :code="code" :installs="installs" />
</template>

import { html } from 'lit' import { DsElement, define } from '@/elements/lib/element' import styles from 'virtual:tw' // AgentWindow.vue as : the website's agent at work (HomeStepViz's last window), large, as the // agents page opens it: the ask, what was added to context, then what the agent did, one under the other, in the dark // code window. It plays once as it renders (the card settles in, each line rises 8px on its own beat, "Thinking" // shimmers until it turns to "Worked for 1s"); reduced motion shows the end at once. The words come through // attributes (Vue's `title` is `heading`); the `mark` slot replaces the brand mark. /** * @summary An agent at work in the dark code window, played once. * @slot mark - Replaces the brand mark in the window's bar. */ export class AgentWindow extends DsElement { static styles = [DsElement.styles, styles] static properties = { heading: {}, tag: {}, ask: {}, answer: {}, tool: {}, source: {} } /** The window's title (Vue's `title`). */ heading = 'Your agent' tag = 'MCP' ask = 'How do refunds work?' answer = 'Refunds are available for 30 days.' tool = 'Search' source = 'Refunds' render() { return html`
${this.heading} ${this.tag}

${this.ask}

Conare added to context

Thinking… Worked for 1s

Called ${this.tool} in docs. ${this.answer}

Source ${this.source}

` } } define('agent-window', AgentWindow)

   - Any other client: it is a remote MCP server at ${MCP} and sign-in is OAuth.

2. List my namespaces with list_namespaces. I connected contracts, slack, crm.
3. Search Conare for a question those documents answer, such as a recent decision or a contract term. Show me the answer and the documents it came from.

const panel = document.getElementById('agent-prompt')
panel.prompt = prompt
panel.code = code
